tools.description: Put a music influence field in the scene. Give it a `source` to make it follow a node or entity -- a character carrying the music with them -- and `tags` to say which entities it governs.

Use it to check a shot frames its subject before trusting that it does -- a camera pointed at nothing reports nothing rather than looking fine. Without `time` or `frame` it reads the camera the last frame used, the same as camera.get, so after moving the camera let a frame happen before asking what it sees. With `time` (or `frame` at `fps`) it evaluates the session's project as it is now -- unsaved edits included -- on a fresh offline engine at that time, exactly as a render's frame there is evaluated (history seek), so the rectangle is the one render.capture will draw: use it on a host that runs no frames (avgen serve). With `width` and `height` each rectangle is also given in pixels.

tools.description: Copy a stem (one part of the song: drums, bass, ...) into the open project's assets/audio/stems/, record it in assets/manifest.json, and analyse it beside the mix. 'op' says how it meets the parameter's value: add is the usual choice, multiply scales it, replace overwrites it. Use attackMs/decayMs to smooth a jumpy source, and an envelope to turn a momentary event such as music.drop into something that decays rather than flashing for one frame. The route is bound immediately and the result says whether it resolved.

tools.description: Run the live scene profiler (avgen --live-profile) on a scratch copy of the project, in a child process, and return its record (schema avgen.liveprofile/1): frame statistics against the target's budget, the critical path (GPU, CPU or sync), GPU time by category, CPU time by stage, resources, and optimization candidates with ESTIMATED savings (and MEASURED ones when verifyCandidates > 0). Headless by default (deterministic, no present); "live" opens windows and measures the real loop. Seconds to minutes. The editor keeps rendering meanwhile, so the GPU is shared and the numbers are contended: for numbers to quote, run the command with the editor closed.

deep.description: the deep mode: 5 s warm-up cap and 20 s measured (default false)

quality.description: auto, a level (ultra..emergency) or a profile (quality, balanced, performance); default auto

tools.description: Search lever combinations (avgen --live-profile --optimize, headless, on a scratch copy) for the least MEASURED visual change that reaches the target (budget x 0.9). Every single lever is measured for time (A/B) and picture (ORIGINAL vs OPTIMIZED: pixel, SSIM, edge, luminance incl. matched, temporal, inside the hero boxes); combinations are ESTIMATED from the singles and then MEASURED. Heroes are never degraded by default. With apply=true the chosen levers are added to the project's live ceilings when the answer arrives (never the scene; performance.set_live_quality clearOverrides undoes it). Minutes. The editor shares the GPU meanwhile.

apply.description: add the chosen levers to the project's ceilings (default false)

Never edits the scene; heroes exempt. The answer lists what was applied with its measured saving and visual change. Minutes.

tools.description: Render one frame of the project as it is in this session -- unsaved edits included; nothing is saved -- to a PNG (or EXR, by the path's extension), through the same offline render path a sequence uses, so the frame hash equals that frame's hash in a render.start sequence. Give `frame` (at `fps`) or `time` (seconds); neither is time 0. `history: play` (the default) first renders and discards every frame from 0, so the frame has the history a play-through had (cost grows with the time); `seek` jumps there, which is fast but may differ slightly on stateful content (envelopes, simulations). Returns a job id at once: job.wait for the result (frame hash, file sha256, timing). The size, rate and tier default to the project's render settings.

tools.description: Edit the scene by applying an RFC 6902 JSON Patch to its document (document.get {document: scene}), then rebuilding the composition from the result. One contract for every structural edit: add a light (`{op: add, path: /lights/-, value: {...}}`), a node (`/nodes/-`), change a node's tint (`/nodes/<i>/tint`), remove anything. Refused with INVALID_ARGUMENTS and details.pointer when an operation does not apply, when the result has a schema error it did not have before, or when it adds a key the engine does not read; nothing is changed then. Keys the patch does not touch are kept, including `_` notes and unknown top-level keys. The session's parameter overrides survive the rebuild: each is re-applied unless the patch set the value the document carries (overrides.yielded lists those). Routes are kept. dryRun checks the patch, builds the result on a private engine and changes nothing. It runs in the call's transaction, so transaction.rollback restores the pre-patch document. A rebuild restarts entity simulations; a live host refuses it while a show runs.
